skip_reason: Existing-move logistics only — not a sales call. The customer opened with 'I just need to call and confirm some of the details for my upcoming move'; she had already booked online for the 12th. The entire call is Rance pulling up her record, verifying home size, box count, large items, walk distance and unload access against what was already on file, and re-confirming the 12:30-2:30 arrival window. No quote was given, no pricing, clock, estimate or differentiator content was in scope, and there was no booking to attempt because the job was already on the schedule. Grading it against the 85-point scorecard would produce a meaningless score.
top_strength: Caught a duplicate booking on the account — 'it looks like I've got two requests for you, one for the nineteenth and one for the twelfth' — and confirmed with the customer that only the 12th was real, which prevented a wasted crew dispatch.
coaching_note: Not graded — confirmation call on an already-booked move. Two notes for the record if this call type ever gets its own rubric: he asked 'Have you confirmed your move yet?' right after she had already said she booked online and had been called about it, and there was a visible pause fumbling the record lookup ('Thinking here. Sorry.'). Otherwise clean, fast, and reassuring.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and easy word choice ('Fantastic', 'Awesome', 'No worries', 'Yes ma'am'), and he acknowledged her Google-fiber scheduling conflict rather than plowing past it; the customer stayed positive throughout and closed with 'thank you so much'.
